title: Glorious Revolution, Union and Queen Anne
welcome_lead: From the Restoration to the Hanoverian succession.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Cavalier Parliament (1661-79) passed the Clarendon Code restraining Dissenters. The Test Act (1673) drove James, Duke of York, out of public office. The Popish Plot (1678) and Exclusion Crisis energised Whigs and Tories. Charles ruled without Parliament 1681-85.

James II's Declaration of Indulgence (1687, 1688), the prosecution of the Seven Bishops (1688) and the birth of his son (10 June 1688) provoked seven leading peers to invite William of Orange. William landed at Torbay (5 November 1688). James fled in December. The Convention Parliament's Bill of Rights (December 1689) and the Toleration Act (1689) defined the settlement. The Mutiny Act (1689) required annual parliamentary renewal of the army.

William died (March 1702) and Anne succeeded. The Act of Settlement (1701) ensured the Hanoverian succession. The War of the Spanish Succession (1701-13/14) brought Marlborough's victories at Blenheim (1704) and Ramillies (1706). The Acts of Union (1707) joined England and Scotland; Anne died 1 August 1714 and was succeeded by George I of Hanover.

mcqs.q: Why is 1688 called the Glorious Revolution?
options: It was glorious because no one died anywhere in the conflict.
Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
William of Orange was Charles II's son and inherited the throne.
Parliament invited William of Orange to replace the Catholic James II, with little bloodshed in England, establishing parliamentary supremacy and the 1689 Bill of Rights.

mcqs.q: Why did Huguenots migrate to England from the 1680s?
options: Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
Louis XIV's 1685 revocation of the Edict of Nantes ended toleration of French Protestants; many fled persecution to Protestant England, bringing skills like silk weaving.
Huguenots came to England because France was poorer than England.
Huguenots were Catholic refugees fleeing Cromwell.

mcqs.q: Why did the American colonies rebel against Britain?
options: Disputes over taxation without representation after the Seven Years' War, growing colonial identity, and British attempts to tighten imperial control on previously autonomous colonies.
Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
The colonists rebelled because they were heavily oppressed and impoverished.
Huguenots were Catholic refugees fleeing Cromwell.
